title: Staged VPC control plane pivot with health-gated traffic quotas
creator: Asha Nair
body:
Summary:
We need a safe, automated path to upgrade control plane components in VPC/private deployments that minimizes customer impact and does not require manual intervention for most upgrades. This ticket defines a staged "pivot" approach that introduces traffic quotas and health gating at the VPC routing level, plus Terraform module changes and end-to-end tests to enable reliable canary-style upgrades across private control planes.

Goals:
- Allow rolling upgrades of control plane services (api-server, operator, syncer) inside customer VPCs with minimal downtime and reversible rollouts.
- Run an automated canary that gradually shifts production traffic from old to new control plane instances in configurable increments (default 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%).
- Enforce health gates using application-level and infra-level signals (API error rate, 99th latency, control-plane probe pass rate, operator reconciliation errors).
- Make the upgrade fully driven by Terraform + orchestration controller (no manual SSH/console steps for standard upgrades).
- Provide clear rollback semantics and automated fallback when a gate fails.

Design notes (high level):
1) Traffic pivot primitive: add a new Terraform-managed resource in the private control plane module (redwood_vpc_controlplane_pivot) that models a traffic allocation resource. This will create/modify a Layer-7 routing object (Nginx/Envoy config or cloud LB rule) that accepts a weight map for endpoint sets (old-version pool, new-version pool). The resource exposes desired_percentage and a status subresource reported back to the orchestration controller (via the private control plane control channel).

2) Health gating engine: implement an orchestration controller (stateless k8s Job within control plane operator) that reads the pivot resource and performs staged increases. The controller evaluates a configurable set of metrics pulled from the control plane metrics exporter and console traces:
   - error_rate_1m (api-server): threshold default 0.5%
   - p99_latency_1m (api-server): threshold default +200ms relative to baseline
   - operator_reconciliations_failed_5m: threshold 1
   - kvcache_miss_ratio_1m: threshold 5% above baseline
   - system_probe_success_rate: must be >= 98%
If any gate fails during a step, we immediately pivot back to the previous allocation and mark the rollout as FAILED.

3) Terraform module changes:
   - Add a new module variable `pivot_enabled` (default false) and `pivot_defaults` (map: step_percentages, step_interval_seconds, rollback_on_failure).
   - Implement resource redwood_vpc_pivot (provider-based custom resource for supported on-prem/in-cloud LB). Where provider is not available, fall back to a traffic-control sidecar pattern.
   - Output artifacts: pivot_id, pivot_status_endpoint, pivot_history (ids).

4) Observability and audit: every staged change writes an audit event to the customer’s control plane audit log (via existing log sink). We also emit rollout metrics to the Redwood Console: rollout_percentage, step_duration_seconds, gate_pass/fail, rollback_count. Console will render per-upgrade timeline and allow operator-triggered abort/force-complete.

5) Rollback semantics: two flavors:
   - automated rollback: controller detects gate failure -> perform immediate revert to last stable allocation -> mark upgrade FAILED -> emit incident note and diagnostic snapshot.
   - expedited rollback: operator uses console or API to set `pivot_desired=0` for new pool to shift traffic back quickly.

6) Safety and limits:
   - Limit maximum concurrent canaries per VPC (default 1) to prevent multiple simultaneous partial pivots.
   - Minimum steady-state interval between steps (configurable).
   - Also allow a "dry-run" flag where all changes are scaffolded but traffic remains pinned to old pool.

Implementation plan (phases):
Phase 1 (prototype) - 2 weeks:
  - Create traffic pivot resource prototype for AWS ALB/Envoy and a simple sidecar fallback for on-prem customers.
  - Build controller that performs a single-step pivot and can revert.
  - Add Terraform variables and outputs to private modules.
Phase 2 (canary automation) - 2 weeks:
  - Extend controller to staged steps and gating logic.
  - Integrate with metrics exporter and add default thresholds.
  - Emit rollout metrics to console (prototype dashboard).
Phase 3 (hardening + tests) - 2 weeks:
  - Cross-VPC integration tests (local infra harness + small on-prem sim).
  - Chaos test scenarios (late start, node flapping).
  - Security review and KMS handling for any control channel secrets.
Phase 4 (gradual rollout) - 1 week:
  - Roll out pivot_enabled default=false. Enable for internal staging customers first, then controlled beta.

Testing matrix and acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests for Terraform provider shim and pivot resource behavior.
- Integration test: full upgrade flow in staging VPC with API traffic replay; must complete to 100% for happy path within configured window.
- Failure injection test: cause API error rate spike above threshold at step 25% -> controller must revert to 0% for new pool and flag FAILED.
- Non-regression: existing private deployments without pivot_enabled should behave unchanged.

Operational playbook (short):
- Start upgrade via console or CLI (set new control plane image tag in module and enable pivot).
- Monitor rollout metrics in Console. If gate fails, controller will auto-revert; on revert open incident and attach diagnostic snapshot (logs, k8s events, metrics).
- For urgent manual rollback: set pivot_desired=0 or use the console abort button.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- How granular should step percentages be exposed to customers? (Default small set vs fully-customizable list).
- For on-prem customers without a supported LB, sidecar fallback adds complexity and might not match cloud LB semantics. Is that acceptable for beta?
- Whether to allow multi-canary per VPC for different control plane subcomponents (api-server vs operator) or enforce single concurrent canary.

Checklist (next actions):
- [ ] Draft Terraform schema and provider hooks for redwood_vpc_pivot (owner: Daniel)
- [ ] Prototype Envoy/ALB weighted routing changes (owner: Sima Patel)
- [ ] Implement minimal controller loop + metrics consumer (owner: Daniel)
- [ ] Add Console dashboard stub and rollout metrics (owner: Priya Singh)
- [ ] Security review kickoff for control channel secrets (owner: Infosec)

Activity log / updates:
2026-02-28 (Asha Nair): Created initial ticket after design sync with product. Captured high-level goals and phased plan.
2026-03-02 (Daniel Park): PoC notes: implemented a local Envoy config generator that accepts two upstream pools and weights. Works in staging; needs integration with k8s admission for dynamic updates.
2026-03-04 (Sima Patel): ALB weighted target groups prototype shows slightly different failover semantics; noted need for health check alignment (ALB considers target healthy differently than our system_probe metric). Adding normalization layer to controller.
2026-03-07 (Daniel Park): Added metrics thresholds and baseline collection plan to controller design. Baseline computed from rolling average of last 30m before upgrade start.
2026-03-10 (Priya Singh): Console dashboard stub created; emits rollout_percentage and gate_status events to the UI stream. Need a short-lived token model for dashboard read access in private deployments. Logged as security TODO.
2026-03-12 (Daniel Park): Implemented terraform variable map and basic redwood_vpc_pivot resource skeleton in module branch `feature/pivot-terraform`. Opening draft PR for early review.

comments: 2026-03-05 - @Priya Singh: Suggest adding a metrics sanity check step that verifies we have metric coverage before starting to move traffic. If metrics are missing, the rollout should pause and require manual confirmation.
2026-03-06 - @Daniel Park: Agreed. Added baseline preflight check to the controller plan. Will fail fast if exporter not present.
2026-03-09 - @Sima Patel: For AWS: prefer ALB weighted target groups for cloud customers, but sidecar fallback required for bare-metal. Document differences in the module README.
2026-03-11 - @Evan Liu (Security): KMS policy review required for control channel secrets passed to the controller. Marking security_review_required=true.
2026-03-12 - @Asha Nair: Started internal beta rollout plan. Keep scope limited to staging VPCs (non-production) until we validate rollback timings and observability coverage.
